issues.description: Element: Farm.addAnimal(Animal). In problem_statement.md the UML lists addAnimal with '-' indicating private visibility (UML line showing '- addAnimal(animal: Animal):void'). However, the example usage in the template Main.java (commented code) calls farm.addAnimal(...) (template Main.java lines with farm.addAnimal calls), and the reference solution defines addAnimal as public (solution Farm.java: public void addAnimal(Animal animal)). This contradiction between the UML (private) and both the intended API/use (public) will confuse students about the required access level and whether they should be able to add animals from outside Farm (e.g., in Main or tests).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended visibility explicit and consistent: update the UML in problem_statement.md to mark addAnimal as public (use '+' instead of '-'), or add a short note in the textual specification stating that addAnimal must be public so it can be called from Main and by tests. This preserves the pedagogical intent (students should be able to add animals) while removing the UML contradiction.
